items.title: Activation of Amino Acids and the Phases of Translation

source_refs.note: Activation of amino acids and the three phases of translation (PDF 137-140); Figures 19.17 to 19.20 are replaced by original diagrams.

blocks.text: Before protein synthesis the building units are prepared: specific tRNAs attach to specific amino acids to make aminoacyl-tRNAs (aa-tRNA). The enzyme aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase does this; there are 20 kinds, each binding one amino acid and recognising the tRNAs with anticodons for it. The aa-tRNA delivers the amino acid to the ribosome.

blocks.alt: Left: a large green enzyme, aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase, holding an amino acid in one pocket and a tRNA in another, with the tRNA's anticodon end inside the enzyme. An arrow leads to the released aminoacyl-tRNA, the amino acid joined to the top of the tRNA, ready to participate in protein synthesis.
blocks.caption: Figure 19.17: Activation of amino acids (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 19.17).
blocks.long_description: Labels: Amino acid, tRNA, Anticodon, Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase, Aminoacyl-tRNA, Ready to participate in protein synthesis.

items: The aa-tRNA carrying the first amino acid binds the small ribosomal subunit, a step controlled by an initiation factor. In prokaryotes the first amino acid is N-formyl-methionine; in eukaryotes it is unmodified methionine.
Another initiation factor attaches the 5' end of the mRNA to the small subunit, placing the anticodon of the aa-tRNA over the first codon, AUG.
The large subunit joins. The initiation complex now has both subunits, the first aa-tRNA, the mRNA and the factors.

blocks.caption: Sites on the ribosome
rows: where the first aa-tRNA sits and peptide bonds form

blocks.text: Along the mRNA the sites lie in the order E-P-A from 5' to 3', because the ribosome moves towards the 3' end.

blocks.alt: Left: the smaller ribosomal subunit with mRNA and the aminoacyl-tRNA carrying Met, its anticodon UAC paired with the start codon AUG. A green arrow leads to the initiation complex: the larger subunit added, with the Met-tRNA in the P site between an empty E site and an empty A site.
blocks.caption: Figure 19.18: Initiation phase of translation (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 19.18).
blocks.long_description: Labels: Aminoacyl tRNA, Smaller subunit, mRNA, Larger subunit, E site, P site, A site, Initiation complex, Met, UAC, AUG, 5', 3'.

items: The next aa-tRNA, with the matching anticodon and amino acid, binds the A site with the help of an elongation factor.
Peptidyl transferase removes the amino acid (first, methionine) from the tRNA at the P site and joins it by a peptide bond to the amino acid of the tRNA at the A site.
The ribosome moves three nucleotides along the mRNA in the 5' to 3' direction (translocation).
The tRNA carrying the chain shifts from the A site to the P site, a new codon is exposed at A, and the empty tRNA moves to E and leaves.
These steps repeat until a stop codon reaches the A site.

blocks.alt: Seven numbered steps round a cycle on the mRNA AUG CUG UCU: (1) the Leu-tRNA (anticodon GAC) enters the A site next to the Met-tRNA in the P site; (2) Met is transferred to Leu, forming a peptide bond; (3) the ribosome moves one codon, the empty tRNA moves to the E site and leaves while the Ser-tRNA (anticodon AGA) arrives; (4) Ser-tRNA binds the A site; (5) the Met-Leu chain is transferred to Ser; (6) the ribosome moves on and the empty tRNA leaves; (7) the process repeats for all codons.
blocks.caption: Figure 19.19: Elongation phase of translation (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 19.19).
blocks.long_description: Each frame shows the larger and smaller subunits, the E, P and A sites, the tRNAs with their anticodons UAC, GAC, AGA and the growing chain Met, Leu, Ser.

blocks.text: When a stop codon is at the A site no aa-tRNA comes, because no tRNA has an anticodon for a stop codon. A protein called a release factor recognises the stop codon and releases the polypeptide from the tRNA at the P site; the tRNA is released and the ribosomal subunits separate from the mRNA.

blocks.alt: Left: the ribosome with a tRNA (anticodon ACC) on UGG in the P site carrying the chain Met-Leu-Ser-Trp and the stop codon UAA in the A site; a release factor approaches. Middle: the release factor sits in the A site and the polypeptide is freed from the tRNA. Below: the polypeptide, the larger subunit, the smaller subunit, the tRNA and the release factor separate from the mRNA.
blocks.caption: Figure 19.20: Termination phase of translation (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 19.20).
blocks.long_description: Labels: Release factor, Stop codon, Polypeptide, Larger subunit, Smaller subunit, tRNA, mRNA, E site, A site, 5', 3'.
